correctness.rationale: Let A,B,C denote part magnetizations in K_{n,n,n}; the exact flip energy is Delta E=2Js(t-(B+C)) in part A. Uniform signs force inequalities; a mixed part forces t=B+C. Classifying zero, one, two and three mixed parts yields the displayed exact N_n(t), including t=0 and t=2n discontinuities, with binomial multiplicities over labeled spin assignments. Strict minima require uniform parts and strict inequalities. A nonground mixed weak minimum has a zero-cost first flip and an opposite-sign spin in another mixed part that then lowers energy by 4J. At t=2k, fixed k, the n+k parity controls the three-mixed binomial-cube term, establishing normalized complexity 0 versus log 2; at t=0 parity gives log2/3 versus log2. Independently recomputed magnetization-level counts and small spin enumerations support formula; full proof covers every n>=1 and real field h.
